Algebra I · Lesson 9.3

Factoring ax² + bx + c

Solve this lesson →All lessons

The quadratic 2x2+7x+32x2+7x+3 factors as (2x+1)(x+3)(2x+1)(x+3). Expand to check, 2x2+6x+x+3=2x2+7x+32x2+6x+x+3=2x2+7x+3. What is new is the leading term. 2x22x2 is the product of the two leading terms, so the leading coefficient must also be split between the factors, and the middle coefficient depends on that split as well as on the constants.

Problem
Factor 5x2+29x+205x2+29x+20. Since 55 is prime, the leading terms can only be 5x5x and xx, so the factorization has the shape (5x+q)(x+s)(5x+q)(x+s) with qq and ss positive whole numbers. Enter qq, the constant beside 5x5x.
Show a hint
  • The leading split is forced, so only the two constants are unknown. List the positive factor pairs of 2020, keeping both orders of each pair, since swapping the constants changes the middle term.
  • Check each candidate on its cross sum 5s+q5s+q, which must equal 2929. The pair with q=20q=20 beside 5x5x gives 2525, close but wrong, so keep going.
Show the full solution
The cross sum 5s+q5s+q must equal 2929. Among the factor pairs of 2020, the pair q=4q=4, s=5s=5 gives 5⋅5+4=295⋅5+4=29, so 5x2+29x+20=(5x+4)(x+5)5x2+29x+20=(5x+4)(x+5) and q=4q=4​. The swapped order q=5q=5, s=4s=4 gives 2525 instead, which is why each pair is checked in both orders.
Problem
Factor 11x2+39x−2011x2+39x−20. The split of 1111 is forced, so the shape is (11x+q)(x+s)(11x+q)(x+s). The product qs=−20qs=−20 is negative, so qq and ss have opposite signs. Enter the negative constant.
Show a hint
  • The cross sum 11s+q11s+q must equal +39+39, a large positive number, so the positive term must be 11s11s. That makes ss positive and qq negative.
  • Test the factor pairs of 2020 with ss positive and qq negative, checking the cross sum 11s+q11s+q against 3939 each time.
Show the full solution
With ss positive and qq negative, the pair q=−5q=−5, s=4s=4 gives the cross sum 11⋅4−5=3911⋅4−5=39, so 11x2+39x−20=(11x−5)(x+4)11x2+39x−20=(11x−5)(x+4) and the negative constant is −5−5​. Fixing the signs first cut the candidate list in half, since a cross sum as large as +39+39 is out of reach when ss is negative.
Key idea
Three conditions. Distributing twice, (px+q)(rx+s)=prx2+psx+qrx+qs(px+q)(rx+s)=prx2+psx+qrx+qs. Matched against ax2+bx+cax2+bx+c, three conditions are read off. The leading terms multiply to the leading coefficient, pr=apr=a. The constants multiply to the constant, qs=cqs=c. The middle coefficient is the sum of the two cross products, ps+qr=bps+qr=b. When a=1a=1 the split is p=r=1p=r=1 and the cross sum is just q+sq+s, 9.2's sum clue. For any other aa the middle depends on how aa is split, so a candidate is a choice of both pairs together, judged on its cross sum.
Problem
Factor 25x2+75x+5425x2+75x+54. Now the leading terms can split as 25x25x and xx or as 5x5x and 5x5x, and both splits have to be searched. Both constants are positive. Enter the larger of the two constants in the factorization.
Show a hint
  • The constant pairs to test are 1⋅541⋅54, 2⋅272⋅27, 3⋅183⋅18 and 6⋅96⋅9, each one usable in either order. Check every candidate on its cross sum against 7575.
  • In the (25x+q)(x+s)(25x+q)(x+s) rows the cross sum is 25s+q25s+q, and the smallest one those pairs give is 7777, which is already above 7575. In the (5x+q)(5x+s)(5x+q)(5x+s) rows it is 5(q+s)5(q+s), so q+s=15q+s=15 with qs=54qs=54.
Show the full solution
Pairing the larger constant with 25x25x gives cross sums 7979, 7777, 9393 and 159159, and swapping each pair only raises the sum, so the 25x25x and xx split is out. In the (5x+q)(5x+s)(5x+q)(5x+s) split the cross sum is 5(q+s)=755(q+s)=75, so q+s=15q+s=15 with qs=54qs=54, and the pair is 66 and 99. So 25x2+75x+54=(5x+6)(5x+9)25x2+75x+54=(5x+6)(5x+9) and the larger constant is 99​. When the two leading terms are equal, the condition on the constants is exactly 9.2's sum and product search.
Problem
Every candidate for 5x2+53x+725x2+53x+72 has the shape (5x+q)(x+s)(5x+q)(x+s) with qq and ss positive and qs=72qs=72, and counting order there are twelve such pairs. The middle coefficient 5353 is odd. How many of the twelve candidates survive that one observation?
Show a hint
  • The cross sum is 5s+q5s+q. Work out its parity when qq and ss are both even, using the fact that 5s5s has the same parity as ss.
  • When qq and ss are both even the cross sum is even, and 5353 is odd. Count the ordered pairs of 7272 with both entries even, then subtract from twelve.
Show the full solution
Since 5s5s has the parity of ss, the cross sum 5s+q5s+q is even whenever qq and ss are both even, and an even sum cannot equal 5353. Both odd is impossible, since qs=72qs=72 is even. The all-even ordered pairs are 2⋅362⋅36, 4⋅184⋅18, 6⋅126⋅12 and their swaps, six in all, and removing them from the twelve leaves 66​. One survivor checks, 5⋅9+8=535⋅9+8=53, so 5x2+53x+72=(5x+8)(x+9)5x2+53x+72=(5x+8)(x+9).
Key idea
The organized search. List the factor pairs of aa for the leading terms and the factor pairs of cc for the constants. A candidate is one pair from each list and nothing else, and it passes only when its cross sum ps+qrps+qr equals bb. Both lists are finite, so the search finishes. 9.2's sign reasoning applies unchanged, and two more filters come from bb. An odd bb is impossible when every entry is even, since both cross products would be even, and a small bb is impossible when both cross products are large. Both filters cut candidates before any cross sum is worked out.

The first step has not changed. Before any lists get written, pull out the greatest common numeric factor and keep it in front. Sometimes what remains is monic, and the whole problem is back in 9.2's shorter search. Sometimes the remaining leading coefficient is smaller but still above 11, and both lists are shorter for it.

Problem
Factor 30x2−156x−14430x2−156x−144 completely. Written as g(5x+q)(x+s)g(5x+q)(x+s), where gg is the greatest common numeric factor, enter ss.
Show a hint
  • All three coefficients are divisible by 66. Take the 66 out first. The quadratic that remains has leading coefficient 55, smaller but above 11, so a search is still needed.
  • Factor 5x2−26x−245x2−26x−24 as (5x+q)(x+s)(5x+q)(x+s). The constant is negative, so qq and ss have opposite signs, and the cross sum 5s+q5s+q must equal −26−26.
Show the full solution
The greatest common factor is 66, leaving 6(5x2−26x−24)6(5x2−26x−24). The constant is negative, so qq and ss have opposite signs, and q=4q=4, s=−6s=−6 gives the cross sum 5(−6)+4=−265(−6)+4=−26, so 30x2−156x−144=6(5x+4)(x−6)30x2−156x−144=6(5x+4)(x−6) and s=−6s=−6​. Taking the 66 out first made every number in the search smaller. The leading coefficient stayed above 11, so a search was still needed, just on easier numbers.
Problem
Factor 81x2−10081x2−100 into two binomials with integer coefficients. There is no middle term to search on, and both end terms are perfect squares, so this is one of 9.1's identities rather than a candidate list. The two constants are opposites. Enter the positive one.
Show a hint
  • No candidate search is needed here. Expand (9x+q)(9x−q)(9x+q)(9x−q) with the double distribution and see which terms cancel.
  • The expansion leaves 81x2−q281x2−q2, so q2=100q2=100, and qq is the positive choice.
Show the full solution
Since 81x2=(9x)281x2=(9x)2 and 100=102100=102, the conjugate identity gives 81x2−100=(9x+10)(9x−10)81x2−100=(9x+10)(9x−10), so q=10q=10​. Expanding, the cross products 90x90x and −90x−90x sum to zero, which is why the middle term is missing.
Key idea
Common factor first, then identities. After the numeric factor is out, check the two identity shapes before writing any lists. Both of 9.1's identities apply with axax as the first term. A difference of two perfect square terms is a conjugate product, 9x2−49=(3x)2−72=(3x+7)(3x−7)9x2−49=(3x)2−72=(3x+7)(3x−7). A trinomial whose end terms are perfect squares, with a middle term twice the product of their roots, is a perfect square, 25x2+30x+9=(5x+3)225x2+30x+9=(5x+3)2, since 2⋅5x⋅3=30x2⋅5x⋅3=30x. A quadratic recognized this way is factored on sight, with no candidate list at all.

An empty search is still a proof. In 3x2+4x+53x2+4x+5 the only leading split is 3x3x and xx, and the constants must be the positive pair 11 and 55. (3x+1)(x+5)(3x+1)(x+5) has cross sum 16x16x, (3x+5)(x+1)(3x+5)(x+1) has cross sum 8x8x, neither is 4x4x, and no integer factorization exists. Quadratics like this are handled in chapter 11.

Problem
Does 4x2+13x+64x2+13x+6 factor into two binomials with integer coefficients? Run the full search, every leading split against every constant pair, before answering yes or no.
Show a hint
  • Both constants have to be positive, since their product 66 and the middle coefficient 1313 are both positive. Then 44 splits only as 4⋅14⋅1 or 2⋅22⋅2, so the whole list has six candidates.
  • The middle coefficient 1313 is odd, so a candidate whose two cross products are both even is impossible. That removes the (2x+q)(2x+s)(2x+q)(2x+s) row, and checking the rest settles it.
Show the full solution
The (4x+q)(x+s)(4x+q)(x+s) row has cross sums 2525, 1010, 1414, 1111 for (q,s)=(1,6)(q,s)=(1,6), (6,1)(6,1), (2,3)(2,3), (3,2)(3,2), and the (2x+q)(2x+s)(2x+q)(2x+s) row has 1414 and 1010. Both constants had to be positive and 44 splits only as 4⋅14⋅1 or 2⋅22⋅2, so those six are the whole list, and none has cross sum 1313, making the answer nono​.
Fun fact
Emmy Noether's 1921 paper turned factoring itself into a subject. It asked in which number systems every factorization is unique, not how to factor one expression, and much of modern algebra descends from it.
Problem
Solve 4x2+27x−40=04x2+27x−40=0. Factor the left side, then split with the zero product property. Enter the positive root, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The leading 44 splits as 4⋅14⋅1 or 2⋅22⋅2, and a 2x2x paired with 2x2x always has an even cross sum, while 2727 is odd.
  • So the factors have the form (4x+q)(x+s)(4x+q)(x+s), with qs=−40qs=−40 and cross sum 4s+q=274s+q=27. The constant is negative, so qq and ss have opposite signs. Once the factoring is done, set each factor equal to zero on its own.
Show the full solution
The left side factors as 4x2+27x−40=(4x−5)(x+8)4x2+27x−40=(4x−5)(x+8), since the cross products 32x32x and −5x−5x add to 27x27x. By the zero product property either 4x−5=04x−5=0 or x+8=0x+8=0, so the roots are 5445​ and −8−8, and the positive root is 5445​​. The root is a fraction because 4x−5=04x−5=0 is finished by dividing by 44.
Key idea
Fraction roots. By the zero product property, each factor set to zero is a linear equation, and px+q=0px+q=0 gives x=−qpx=−pq​, the constant with its sign flipped, divided by the coefficient of xx. In 9.2 every factor was x+qx+q, so every root was an integer. With the leading coefficient split between the factors, a root is a fraction whenever pp does not divide qq, and that is normal, not a sign of error. Write every fraction root exactly and in lowest terms. Reading the root off a factor without the sign flip, or without the division by pp, is the standard mistake.

The zero product property applies to a product equal to zero and nothing else, so the first move has not changed. When a quadratic equation has terms on both sides, subtract until one side is zero, collect like terms, and only then factor and split. A factored left side proves nothing while the right side is nonzero.

Problem
Solve 5x2+22x=485x2+22x=48. The right side is not zero, and the zero product property applies only to a product that equals zero, so rearrange first, then factor and split. Enter the positive root as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Move 4848 across so the right side is zero. The leading coefficient 55 is prime, so the split of the leading terms is forced.
  • Search (5x+q)(x+s)(5x+q)(x+s) with qs=−48qs=−48, and keep the candidate whose cross products add to 22x22x.
Show the full solution
Moving 4848 across gives 5x2+22x−48=05x2+22x−48=0. Since 55 is prime the leading terms split as 5x5x and xx, and −8−8 with 66 gives cross products 30x30x and −8x−8x, which add to 22x22x, so 5x2+22x−48=(5x−8)(x+6)5x2+22x−48=(5x−8)(x+6). Then 5x−8=05x−8=0 or x+6=0x+6=0, so x=85x=58​ or x=−6x=−6, and the positive root is 8558​​. Checking in the original equation, 5⋅6425+22⋅85=645+1765=485⋅2564​+22⋅58​=564​+5176​=48.
Problem
The first and last terms of 144x2+bx+49144x2+bx+49 are both perfect squares. Find the positive value of bb that makes the whole trinomial the square of a binomial.
Show a hint
  • Start by writing those two terms as squares, 144x2=(12x)2144x2=(12x)2 and 49=7249=72.
  • Expanding (px+q)2(px+q)2 gives p2x2+2pqx+q2p2x2+2pqx+q2, so the middle coefficient is twice the product of the two terms being squared, not just their product.
Show the full solution
The first and last terms are (12x)2(12x)2 and 7272, and with bb positive the trinomial is (12x+7)2=144x2+168x+49(12x+7)2=144x2+168x+49, so b=168b=168​. A common slip is 8484, the product 12⋅712⋅7 without the doubling. The middle term of a square is twice that product, one copy from each cross product.
Key idea
The full pipeline, extended. Rearrange until one side is zero. Pull out the common numeric factor, and xx itself when there is no constant term. Check for a difference of squares or a perfect square with axax as the first term. Otherwise run the organized search, signs first, then the parity and size of bb, then cross sums. Split with the zero product property and reduce every fraction root to lowest terms. That is 9.2's pipeline with one new layer, the split of the leading coefficient. Put a fraction root back into the original equation, since a slip in the split shows up there at once.

You can now take any quadratic with integer coefficients through one finite process, common factor out, identities checked, candidates listed, narrowed, and tested on their cross sums. When an integer factorization exists the process ends on it, and an exhausted list is a proof that none exists. The two closing problems draw on most of it at once.

Problem
Factor 24x2−34x−4524x2−34x−45 into two binomials with integer coefficients, writing both leading coefficients as positive. Since the constant is −45−45, the two constants in the factors have opposite signs, so exactly one of them is negative. Enter that negative constant.
Show a hint
  • Both constants in the factors are odd, since their product is −45−45. The cross products must add to the even number −34−34, and that happens only when the two leading coefficients have the same parity.
  • Try the split 4⋅64⋅6 of 2424 against the odd factor pairs of 4545, with signs chosen so the cross products add to −34−34.
Show the full solution
Both constants are odd, since their product is −45−45, so each cross product has the parity of its leading coefficient, and those add to the even −34−34. Both leading coefficients are therefore even, leaving the splits 2⋅122⋅12 and 4⋅64⋅6 of 2424. No odd pair of 4545 fits 2⋅122⋅12, and 4⋅64⋅6 with constants −9−9 and 55 gives cross products −54x−54x and 20x20x, so 24x2−34x−45=(4x−9)(6x+5)24x2−34x−45=(4x−9)(6x+5) and the negative constant is −9−9​. With an odd constant and an even middle coefficient, only the even splits of aa are possible, which is a fast first cut.
Problem
Solve 36x2+13x−40=036x2+13x−40=0. There are five splits of 3636 and four factor pairs of 4040, so narrow the list with sign and parity reasoning before trying candidates. Enter the negative root as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The middle coefficient 1313 is odd, so one cross product is odd and one is even. An all even split of 3636 or an all even factor pair of 4040 makes both of them even.
  • After the parity cut the splits still open are 1⋅361⋅36, 3⋅123⋅12, 4⋅94⋅9 and the pairs 1⋅401⋅40, 5⋅85⋅8. The constant is negative, so the two cross product sizes differ by 1313.
Show the full solution
Factoring gives 36x2+13x−40=(4x+5)(9x−8)36x2+13x−40=(4x+5)(9x−8), so 4x+5=04x+5=0 or 9x−8=09x−8=0, and the roots are x=−54x=−45​ and x=89x=98​, making the negative root −54−45​​. The search is short because 1313 is odd, which rules out every all even split of 3636 and every all even factor pair of 4040.

So far every root in this chapter was found the same way, factor first, then read each root off its factor. Lesson 9.4, Roots, Sums, and Products, works without that step. The sum and the product of a quadratic's roots can be read straight from its coefficients, so questions about the roots can be answered without ever finding them. That is new.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Factor 5x2+31x+445x2+31x+44. The leading coefficient is prime, so the two factors can only begin with 5x5x and xx. Enter the constant in the factor whose leading term is 5x5x.
Show the solution
The shape is (5x+q)(x+s)(5x+q)(x+s) with qs=44qs=44 and cross sum 5s+q=315s+q=31. The pair q=11q=11, s=4s=4 gives 5⋅4+11=315⋅4+11=31, so 5x2+31x+44=(5x+11)(x+4)5x2+31x+44=(5x+11)(x+4) and the constant beside 5x5x is 1111​. The swapped order q=4q=4, s=11s=11 gives 5959, which is why order matters.
Practice
Factor 11x2−38x−2411x2−38x−24. The leading coefficient is prime, so the linear terms can only be 11x11x and xx. Enter the negative one of the two constants in the factored form.
Show the solution
In (11x+q)(x+s)(11x+q)(x+s) with qs=−24qs=−24, the middle coefficient is 11s+q11s+q, and s=−4s=−4 with q=6q=6 gives −44+6=−38−44+6=−38. So 11x2−38x−24=(11x+6)(x−4)11x2−38x−24=(11x+6)(x−4), and the negative constant is −4−4​. Flipping both signs gives (11x−6)(x+4)(11x−6)(x+4), whose middle coefficient is +38+38, the right size and the wrong sign.
Practice
Factor 6x2+41x+306x2+41x+30 into two binomials with positive integer coefficients. The leading coefficient is not prime, so there is more than one way to split it between the two factors. Enter the smaller of the two constants.
Show the solution
Splitting the leading coefficient as 6⋅16⋅1 gives 6x2+41x+30=(6x+5)(x+6)6x2+41x+30=(6x+5)(x+6), with middle coefficient 6⋅6+5=416⋅6+5=41 and constants multiplying to 3030, so the smaller constant is 55​. The balanced split (2x+q)(3x+s)(2x+q)(3x+s) is a dead end, since no factor pair of 3030 makes 2s+3q=412s+3q=41.
Practice
Factor 9x2−31x−709x2−31x−70 into two binomials with integer coefficients. The middle coefficient is not a multiple of 33, which rules out the split with 3x3x in both factors, since that split makes every cross sum a multiple of 33. Enter the positive constant.
Show the solution
In the (3x+q)(3x+s)(3x+q)(3x+s) split every cross sum is 3(q+s)3(q+s), a multiple of 33, and −31−31 is not, so the shape is (9x+q)(x+s)(9x+q)(x+s) with 9s+q=−319s+q=−31 and qs=−70qs=−70. The pair q=14q=14, s=−5s=−5 gives 9(−5)+14=−319(−5)+14=−31, so 9x2−31x−70=(9x+14)(x−5)9x2−31x−70=(9x+14)(x−5) and the positive constant is 1414​. Ruling out a whole split by divisibility is cheaper than testing its rows one at a time.
Practice
Factor 4x2+31x+604x2+31x+60. The middle coefficient is odd, so the two factors cannot both have an even coefficient on xx, since both cross products would then be even. Enter the constant in the factor whose leading term is 4x4x.
Show the solution
The all-even split is out, so the linear terms are 4x4x and xx. In (4x+q)(x+s)(4x+q)(x+s) with qs=60qs=60, the middle coefficient is 4s+q4s+q, and q=15q=15 with s=4s=4 gives 16+15=3116+15=31. So 4x2+31x+60=(4x+15)(x+4)4x2+31x+60=(4x+15)(x+4), and the constant asked for is 1515​. Checking parity first rules out the 2x2x times 2x2x split before any candidate is expanded.
Practice
Factor 5x2+60x+1605x2+60x+160 completely, pulling out the greatest common numeric factor before any candidate search. Enter the larger of the two constants in the binomials that remain.
Show the solution
Every coefficient is a multiple of 55, so 5x2+60x+160=5(x2+12x+32)5x2+60x+160=5(x2+12x+32). The pair with sum 1212 and product 3232 is 44 and 88, giving 5(x+4)(x+8)5(x+4)(x+8), so the larger constant is 88​. Pulling the 55 out first leaves a monic quadratic, so the sum and product search finishes it with no candidate list to check.
Practice
Each end term of 196x2−169196x2−169 is a perfect square and there is no middle term, so this is the conjugate identity rather than a search. Factor it as (14x+q)(14x−q)(14x+q)(14x−q) with qq positive. What is qq?
Show the solution
Since 196x2=(14x)2196x2=(14x)2 and 169=132169=132, the identity gives 196x2−169=(14x+13)(14x−13)196x2−169=(14x+13)(14x−13), so q=13q=13​. The two cross products are −182x−182x and +182x+182x, which cancel, and that cancellation is why the middle term is missing.
Practice
Does 6x2+5x+46x2+5x+4 factor into two binomials with integer coefficients? Both the constant and the middle coefficient are positive, so both constants would have to be positive. Run every leading split against every constant pair before answering yes or no.
Show the solution
For (6x+q)(x+s)(6x+q)(x+s) the cross sum 6s+q6s+q gives 2525, 1414 and 1010, and for (2x+q)(3x+s)(2x+q)(3x+s) the cross sum 2s+3q2s+3q gives 1111, 1010 and 1414. None of the six equals 55, so the answer is nono​. The search is finite, so coming up empty is a complete answer, and quadratics like this one get their treatment in chapter 11.
Practice
Factor 6x2−17x−1146x2−17x−114 as (6x+q)(x+s)(6x+q)(x+s) with integers qq and ss. The constant term is negative, so qq and ss have opposite signs. Enter qq.
Show the solution
The conditions are qs=−114qs=−114 and 6s+q=−176s+q=−17. Among the factor pairs of 114114, only 66 and 1919 fit, with s=−6s=−6 and q=19q=19 giving 6(−6)+19=−176(−6)+19=−17, so 6x2−17x−114=(6x+19)(x−6)6x2−17x−114=(6x+19)(x−6) and q=19q=19​. The order inside the pair matters, since s=−19s=−19 with q=6q=6 gives 6(−19)+6=−1086(−19)+6=−108 instead.
Practice
Factor 4x2+9x−1004x2+9x−100 as (4x+q)(x+s)(4x+q)(x+s) with integers qq and ss. The constant is large while the middle coefficient is small, so the two cross products very nearly cancel. Enter qq.
Show the solution
The conditions are qs=−100qs=−100 and 4s+q=94s+q=9. The pair s=−4s=−4, q=25q=25 meets both, since 25⋅(−4)=−10025⋅(−4)=−100 and 4(−4)+25=94(−4)+25=9, so 4x2+9x−100=(4x+25)(x−4)4x2+9x−100=(4x+25)(x−4) and q=25q=25​. A 2⋅22⋅2 split of the leading coefficient is impossible here, since (2x+m)(2x+n)(2x+m)(2x+n) has even middle coefficient 2m+2n2m+2n while 99 is odd.
Practice
Each end term of 25x2−kx+8125x2−kx+81 is a perfect square. There is exactly one positive number kk that makes the whole quadratic the square of a binomial. What is kk?
Show the solution
The end terms are (5x)2(5x)2 and 9292, and (5x−9)2=25x2−90x+81(5x−9)2=25x2−90x+81, so k=90k=90​. The middle term of a squared binomial is twice the product of the two terms being squared, so its size here is 2⋅5⋅9=902⋅5⋅9=90, and it is negative because of the minus in 5x−95x−9.
Practice
Solve 9x2+16x−80=09x2+16x−80=0. One root is negative and one is a positive fraction. Enter the positive root as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The conditions qs=−80qs=−80 and 9s+q=169s+q=16 hold for q=−20q=−20, s=4s=4, so 9x2+16x−80=(9x−20)(x+4)9x2+16x−80=(9x−20)(x+4). The zero product property gives 9x−20=09x−20=0 or x+4=0x+4=0, so x=209x=920​ or x=−4x=−4, and the positive root is x=209x=920​​. Checking the middle term, 36x−20x=16x36x−20x=16x.
Practice
Solve 20x2+45x−275=020x2+45x−275=0. A numeric factor comes out of all three terms first, and what remains still has a leading coefficient above 11. Enter the positive root as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Dividing by 55 leaves 4x2+9x−55=04x2+9x−55=0. A 2x2x times 2x2x split would make the middle coefficient even, so the leading terms are 4x4x and xx, and (4x−11)(x+5)(4x−11)(x+5) has cross sum 20−11=920−11=9 with constant −55−55. The roots of 5(4x−11)(x+5)=05(4x−11)(x+5)=0 are 114411​ and −5−5, so the positive root is 114411​​. The factor 55 is never zero, so only the binomials give roots.
Practice
Factor 20x2−89x+8020x2−89x+80 into two binomials with integer coefficients. Enter the constant in the factor whose leading term is 5x5x, sign included.
Show the solution
The split (4x+q)(5x+s)(4x+q)(5x+s) needs qs=80qs=80 and 4s+5q=−894s+5q=−89. The pair q=−5q=−5, s=−16s=−16 fits, since 4(−16)+5(−5)=−64−25=−894(−16)+5(−5)=−64−25=−89, so 20x2−89x+80=(4x−5)(5x−16)20x2−89x+80=(4x−5)(5x−16) and the constant in the 5x5x factor is −16−16​. An odd middle coefficient needs one odd constant, and the only odd divisors of 8080 are 11 and 55, so only two candidates ever need checking.
Practice
Factor 36x2−60x−11936x2−60x−119 into two binomials with integer coefficients, writing both leading coefficients as positive. The constant is negative, so exactly one of the two constants in the factors is negative. Enter that negative constant.
Show the solution
With the split 6⋅66⋅6 the cross sum is 6(q+s)=−606(q+s)=−60, giving q+s=−10q+s=−10 with qs=−119qs=−119, which is the pair 77 and −17−17. Then 36x2−60x−119=(6x+7)(6x−17)36x2−60x−119=(6x+7)(6x−17) and the negative constant is −17−17​. A middle coefficient divisible by 66 makes the split with two equal leading terms worth trying first, since equal leading terms make the cross sum a multiple of them.
Practice
Solve 20x2+51x−90=020x2+51x−90=0. Neither root is a whole number here, which is ordinary once the leading coefficient is above 11. Enter the positive root as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The split (5x+q)(4x+s)(5x+q)(4x+s) with q=−6q=−6 and s=15s=15 has cross sum 5⋅15+4⋅(−6)=515⋅15+4⋅(−6)=51, so (5x−6)(4x+15)=0(5x−6)(4x+15)=0 and the roots are 6556​ and −154−415​, with positive root 6556​​. The root from 5x−6=05x−6=0 is 6556​, not −65−56​, since 5x=65x=6.
Practice
Solve 48x2+26x=5548x2+26x=55. The right side is not zero, and the zero product property needs it to be, so rearrange before factoring. Enter the negative root as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Rearranged, 48x2+26x−55=048x2+26x−55=0. The split (8x+q)(6x+s)(8x+q)(6x+s) with q=11q=11, s=−5s=−5 gives 8(−5)+6⋅11=268(−5)+6⋅11=26, so (8x+11)(6x−5)=0(8x+11)(6x−5)=0 with roots −118−811​ and 5665​. The negative root is −118−811​​. Each factor px+qpx+q contributes the root −q/p−q/p, so a leading coefficient that does not divide its constant leaves a fraction.
